nodes.description: Reduced miRISC effector output is proposed to disturb miRNA-dependent regulation of gene networks that are highly expressed in the developing brain, including transcripts translated locally at synapses. The specific targets, cell types and developmental window are unknown. TNRC6B is expressed in the developing and adult brain, and TNRC6B belongs to a co-expression module of speech-related regulatory genes highly expressed in embryonic human brain.

nodes.description: TNRC6B is a GW182-family scaffold that binds Argonaute proteins through its N-terminal GW repeats and, through its C-terminal silencing domain, recruits the PAN2-PAN3 and CCR4-NOT deadenylase complexes to miRNA targets, causing translational repression and deadenylation-dependent decay. Loss of one copy is proposed to reduce this effector output of the miRNA pathway. That the scaffold function is reduced in patient tissue has not been measured.

biological_processes: miRNA-mediated gene silencing by mRNA destabilization

evidence.reference_title: Identification of novel argonaute-associated proteins.
evidence.snippet: Several known Ago1- and/or Ago2-associated proteins including Dicer were identified, but also two novel factors, the putative RNA helicase MOV10, and the RNA recognition motif (RRM)-containing protein TNRC6B/KIAA1093.

evidence.reference_title: The C-terminal domains of human TNRC6A, TNRC6B, and TNRC6C silence bound transcripts independently of Argonaute proteins.
evidence.snippet: Our findings indicate that TNRC6A, TNRC6B, and TNRC6C are recruited to miRNA targets through an interaction between their N-terminal domain and an Argonaute protein; the TNRC6s then promote translational repression and/or degradation of miRNA targets through a C-terminal silencing domain.

evidence.reference_title: GW182 proteins directly recruit cytoplasmic deadenylase complexes to miRNA targets.
evidence.snippet: We found that human GW182 proteins recruit the PAN2-PAN3 and CCR4-CAF1-NOT deadenylase complexes through direct interactions with PAN3 and NOT1, respectively.

evidence.reference_title: Ago-TNRC6 triggers microRNA-mediated decay by promoting two deadenylation steps.
evidence.snippet: we show that let-7 miRNA-induced silencing complexes (miRISCs), which contain the proteins Argonaute (Ago) and TNRC6 (also known as GW182), trigger very rapid mRNA decay by inducing accelerated biphasic deadenylation mediated by Pan2-Pan3 and Ccr4-Caf1 deadenylase complexes followed by Dcp1-Dcp2 complex-directed decapping in mammalian cells.

evidence.reference_title: Functional dissection of the human TNRC6 (GW182-related) family of proteins.
evidence.snippet: In contrast, the C-terminal domain containing the RNA recognition motif plays a critical role in the silencing mediated by the TNRC6B protein.

evidence.reference_title: The biochemical basis for the cooperative action of microRNAs.
evidence.snippet: Thus, the multivalent binding of TNRC6 enables cooperative binding of miRNA-AGO complexes to target RNAs, thereby explaining the basis of cooperative action.

evidence.reference_title: Phase Transitions in the Assembly and Function of Human miRISC.
evidence.snippet: Phase separation is promoted by multivalent interactions between the glycine/tryptophan (GW)-rich domain of TNRC6B and three evenly spaced tryptophan-binding pockets in the Ago2 PIWI domain.

nodes.description: Heterozygous nonsense, frameshift, splice-site, intragenic or whole-gene deletion alleles remove one functional copy of TNRC6B. Truncating variants upstream of the last exon junction are predicted to undergo nonsense-mediated decay, a synonymous variant that causes exon skipping has been shown to be pathogenic, and a deletion removing exons 2-23 segregates with the phenotype, so reduced TNRC6B dosage is the proposed disease mechanism. Rare missense variants are also reported.
